title: Is it okay to run shirtless in public?
description:
Do you run without a a shirt on ever? Lots of people have opinions on this topic and in some parts of the world it’s something you’re just not allowed to do.

We hear from runners around the world for their take on the decision to run without a shirt one - for both men and women.

And Yijin Shim from BBC Korean tells us about how in South Korea “no shirtless running” signs have been popping up after more runners have been going shirtless in a heatwave.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討民眾在公共場所赤裸上身跑步引發的爭議與文化差異。主持人 Hannah Gelbart 邀請來自倫敦的 Jen 與來自印度的 Hardik 聊聊在酷暑中不穿上衣或僅穿運動內衣跑步的經驗，兩人表示這樣能散熱防磨傷並建立身材自信，但也提及社會規範及性別雙重標準。跑者 Mike 分享自己在義大利威尼斯赤膊跑步時被關切，查了法規才發現當地禁止此行為；BBC 韓語服務的 Yijin Shim 與韓國跑者 Soo-min Lee 則指出，韓國因高溫使赤膊跑步現象增加，雖然無全國法規禁止，但汝矣島漢江公園與南山公園等地已出現禁止赤膊跑步的告示，引發對服儀得體性、體型審美與性別特權的討論。此外，義大利蘇連多等城市亦對在非海灘區域赤膊者開罰最高 500 歐元。節目最後提醒跑者，運動前應先了解當地的法律與文化習俗。
summaryEn: Host Hannah Gelbart explores the debate surrounding running shirtless or in a sports bra during intense heatwaves. Runners Jen from London and Hardik from India share how running without a top offers physical comfort, prevents chafing, and builds body confidence, while acknowledging cultural expectations and gender double standards. American runner Mike Naccarella recounts unknowingly breaking the law by running shirtless in Venice, Italy, highlighting the importance of researching local regulations. BBC Korean's Yijin Shim and runner Soo-min Lee discuss South Korea's heated debate, where high temperatures led to an increase in shirtless runners, prompting parks such as Yeouido Hangang River Park and Namsan Park to put up non-mandatory restriction signs amid discussions over public decorum, body image, and male privilege. With Italian tourist spots like Sorrento imposing fines up to 500 euros for going shirtless away from beaches, the podcast advises runners to always check local laws and etiquette before ditching their shirts.
